title: Plasma and effect site: why the effect lags
intro: A drug taken by mouth is absorbed into the blood (a one-compartment model with first-order absorption), and from the blood it slowly reaches the tissue where it acts, the effect site. Two models run side by side in time: the pharmacokinetic model gives the plasma concentration at each step, and a differential equation, dCe/dt = ke0 (Cp − Ce), carries it to the effect site. Change the dose and the rate ke0 and watch how far the effect-site peak falls behind and below the plasma peak.
ec50Label: EC50 (concentration for half the maximal effect)
plotTitle: Concentration in plasma and at the effect site
